world.register: contemporary nonfiction, behavioral psychology, executive time management, concrete practical scenes

objects.why: The prime source of reactive digital distraction and sudden dopamine notifications.
The core theme of high-value professional output versus trivial busywork.
Clear written goals and priority milestones that focus energy.
Physical paper to-do lists, daily agendas, and the written ABCDE priority matrix.
The morning work ritual and initial start of the focused workday.
The finite daily block of 24 hours and the ticking urgency of key deadlines.
The irreversible passage of focused cognitive energy throughout the day.
The invisible emotional shackles of procrastination, guilt, and perfectionism.
Boundaries protecting deep work blocks from interruptions and endless meetings.
Sudden mental breakthrough when eliminating trivial low-value tasks.

spine.claim: Procrastination is not laziness but an emotional defense mechanism against fear and perfectionism, creating the illusion of productive busyness.
The ABCDE method and forced efficiency require ruthlessly eliminating lower-tier tasks to protect high-leverage focus hours.
Conquering the single most daunting task ('the frog') first thing in the morning fundamentally rewires mental momentum and self-discipline.
Single-handling major projects without context-switching collapses completion time and exponentially multiplies daily output.
Time management is ultimately self-esteem management: taking back your calendar restores self-respect and personal freedom.
